{{Short description|American biostatistician and environmental statistician}}
'''Virginia Marie Lesser''' is an American [[biostatistics|biostatistician]] and [[environmental statistics|environmental statistician]] known for her research on [[non-sampling error]], [[survey methodology]], and agricultural applications of statistics. She is a professor of statistics and chair of the statistics department at [[Oregon State University]].{{r|osu}}

==Education and career==
Lesser completed her Ph.D. in [[biostatistics]] in 1992 at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]]. Her dissertation, ''A Comparison of Periodic Survey Designs Employing Multi-Stage Sampling'', was supervised by William D. Kalsbeek.{{r|mgp}}

At Oregon State, she has been Director of the Survey Research Center since 1993.{{r|src}}
She became the first woman promoted to full professor in statistics at Oregon State, in 2009.{{r|hist}}

==Recognition==
Lesser became a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2010.{{r|fasa}}
She is also an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].{{r|isi}}
